competitors.name: Grocery Outlet
competitors.action: Grocery Outlet plans to debut its first private-label products in Q3, starting in beverage and grocery and targeting about 100 SKUs by year-end. Progressive Grocer reported that CEO RJ Sheedy framed the program around customer value, margin improvement and differentiated NOSH-oriented products. For Real Dough, the signal is that even extreme-value retailers are building own-brand programs that can eventually pressure specialty and freezer sets, not just center-store commodities.

competitors.name: Progressive Grocer Editors' Picks 2026
competitors.action: Progressive Grocer's 2026 Best New Products list highlighted multiple freezer and prepared-food innovation lanes, including Mad Genius Snack Lab frozen mashups, Pulmuone Korean street-food-style mozzarella sticks and Nature's Premium frozen yogurt pearls. The pattern is useful for frozen pizza: retailers are rewarding globally inspired, air-fryer-ready, snackable and texture-forward frozen formats rather than only traditional meal replacements.

competitors.name: Ahold Delhaize USA
competitors.action: Ahold Delhaize USA held its first supplier summit in May, with Grocery Dive reporting focus areas including retail media, agentic commerce, health, sustainability and scaling supplier partnerships across its five banners. For Real Dough, the practical read is that large grocery accounts are making supplier readiness broader than item acceptance: brands need to support omnichannel activation, health cues, sustainability data and retailer-specific growth priorities.
